svg.title: Multivenue engine — live architecture, 2026-09-19
svg.desc: Seven venues stream into a single-writer Rust engine over SPSC rings; eight strategy slots evaluate in-line on the engine thread; every record is appended to PMLR capture; an out-of-process model sidecar bay plugs in over an 82-byte HMAC'd Unix-socket frame through two doors — live fair values into slot 4, or a compiled 256-row ruleset into slot 5. The live-execution arm is built and dark.

text.tspan: actualized 2026-09-19 at the E7 review commit (E1–E7 on top of 49d155d)
(2026-08-29, Stage-2 FINISH), which is kept unmodified as that record
Everything trades PAPER until the operator arms a slot.
The live-execution arm (E1–E6, reviewed + re-tested in E7) is built and REACHABLE:
builds a real HlExchange behind the router (LIVE_ARM_VENUES = [Hyperliquid]); E7 = the TESTNET ramp, mainnet a later ruling.

svg.text: VENUES — 7 VenueId bytes (core-types/src/lib.rs:55-70) · TLS 1.3 via rustls · WebSocket de-framed and unmasked in place
ONE socket + ONE thread per symbol
not a market feed — the byte the
Alchemy RPC rides its own thread and emits Signal, not Tick — it holds no VenueId byte and no tick lane. · Venue REST (keyless, RestBudget 60 req/venue/h) is worker-only and never touches the engine.
INGRESS THREADS — mio + rustls · handwritten byte scanners · no tokio, no serde_json, no allocation after boot
the core map is advisory on the live deployment
sched_setaffinity(2) on Linux is real and kernel-enforced. On macOS — the machine this actually runs on — pin_impl() returns Err(Unsupported) and logs one warning:
every "pinned" thread below floats under the Darwin scheduler (cli/src/pinning.rs:92-99). The engine's own hot loop is never pinned on any platform, on purpose or otherwise.
SPSC RINGS — core-ring::Ring<T,N>, the only ring primitive in the tree · N a power of two · head and tail each own a full 64 B cache line
lane 3 = the HL arm's userFills pump (--exec)

text.tspan: of ring memory total, allocated once at boot and never resized.
— no MPSC type exists anywhere in the workspace; every multi-producer need is

svg.text: solved with one dedicated ring per venue lane. try_push returns Err(value) on a full ring: the ring itself never drops — the ingress caller drops the value and bumps engine_ingress_<venue>_ring_drops_total.
Not core-ring rings, don't conflate: RecentRing<Order|Fill,64> (overwrite-on-wrap, feeds /state + TUI) and TidRing<4096> (Hyperliquid trade-id dedupe inside HlExchange — O(1) since the E7 review).
THE HOT LOOP — Engine::tick(DRAIN_BATCH=256) on the single, unpinned main thread · generic over Strategy, monomorphized, no dyn
capture BEFORE callback · lane 3 carries venue fills on --exec
disp.try_next_fill() — the ONLY live fill source
disp.on_venue_event() first: a roll tells the
okx · deribit → on_depth (the ruleset VM only)
→ on_opt_summary (the VM and one coded member)
drained TO EMPTY, every pass, immediately before
budget 8/pass · TTL re-checked on pop, then shape

Strategy members are struct fields, not threads: slots 0–6 all evaluate in-line, in slot order, inside this one call. StampCtx stamps Order.strategy_id per slot before EngineCtx::submit — that byte is what the exec router reads later.
STRATEGY SLOTS — StrategySet, one u8 enable mask, MAX 8 · BUILT_MASK = 127 (strategy-set/src/lib.rs:178)
what the engine does with it
the first member ever written; still composed into the set
built, OFF in every wrapper mask
evaluated in-line on the engine thread, every tick, from its own crate
evaluated in-line on the engine thread, every tick, from its own crate
evaluated in-line on the engine thread, every tick, from its own crate
quotes the fair value / bias a sidecar pushed; honours paper-only OrderIntent
evaluates the committed ≤256-row table every tick, with no AI in the loop
evaluated in-line on the engine thread, every tick, from its own crate
the next coded member claims it the way the last four each did

text.tspan: the mask is one bit per slot
— the AI pair alone is 48; with one coded member alongside it, 50, 52 or 56; with all three, 62; every built member at once is BUILT_MASK = 127.

svg.text: Which named combinations the wrapper permits is a deployment detail, not an architectural one: scripts/engine-wrapper.sh allow-lists 13 of them, never the first member and never all, and it always passes --paper and never --exec. Two displaced members still boot as standalone arms outside the set; a third has no reachable boot path at all.
EXECUTION — per-slot routing, the E6 risk gate and the live arm, armed only by the two-switch interlock
ExecRoute — per slot, not per process
unknown byte ⇒ Paper. 8 slots × 8 venues, boot-fixed.
LAW E-1: a live slot whose venue bit is clear gets
NoLiveRoute — it NEVER silently falls back to paper.
EXACT same live set or the boot refuses.
The artifact alone arms nothing; the flag alone arms nothing.
--exec is refused for the three standalone non-set arms —
only the composed set arm builds a RoutedDispatcher at all.
what stands between a live order and the venue
LIVE_ARM_VENUES = [Hyperliquid] (exec_boot.rs) — a live slot on any other
venue still refuses the boot. On --exec the bin builds HlExchange
behind RoutedDispatcher, hands it fill lane 3's producer, and refuses
a market-data host and an exchange host on different networks (LAW E-4).
E6: per-order / open / day / instance caps clamp every live submit AND
modify; six sticky halts (reject streak, asset refusals, budget floor,
recon drift, recon STALE, ws gap) cancel-all + write exec.HALT; the arm
runs on the engine thread from on_idle (2 ms pacer), never a worker.
CAPTURE — PMLR v3, one run-<epoch_ns>/ per boot · append-only · torn-tail tolerant · §6.5: capture IS the product, an open failure is a fatal boot error

text.tspan: the writer is write(2), not mmap
— PmlrWriter stages each record into a 64 KiB PreallocatedWriter buffer and write_all()s on buffer-full (core-io/src/lib.rs:87-110).

svg.text: raw libc mmap(PROT_READ, MAP_PRIVATE) with a pointer cast over the mapping, genuinely zero-copy, used by audit-replay / backtest / audit-pnl (core-io/src/pmlr_reader.rs). Header: 64 B, magic PMLR, VERSION 3 since the 09-03 VT1 venue-time fields; v1/v2 still readable.

instrument-manifest.tsv is rewritten EVERY boot and is load-bearing: option and PM-daily ordinals reshuffle per boot by design, so every offline consumer joins by DESCRIPTOR string, never a bare SymbolId.
SymbolId is a u32 bit-pack — venue byte in bits 31..24, per-venue ordinal in 23..0, allocated once at boot from REST discovery, never parsed on the hot path (core-types/src/lib.rs:130-175).

engine-fills.pmlr and engine-orders.pmlr are written by the engine thread itself; every other file is written by its own ingress thread, capture BEFORE the ring push — a ring-dropped tick must still reach the replay log.
MODEL SIDECAR BAY — pluggable, out of process
the engine never links a model runtime, never links Python, and never blocks on a model
outside git · the engine never links it
Every live path it proposed died at a gate.
One lost to a far simpler in-engine
other failed its first gate outright.
a zero-shot forecaster on a lighter
in code, not in a comment
Hundreds of thousands of forecasts across
ten data cells and seventeen shapes, and no
arm clearing the cheapest round-trip fee.
the bay is the reusable part, not the
Slot 7 is free. Generic: everything on the
the payload choice, the pass/fail numbers.
THE RAIL — what every sidecar shares (the P-laws, extracted from both lanes)
candles.db (SQLite WAL) — OHLCV, funding, iv_digest, depth_digest, refdata
PMLR capture by mmap — claude_worker/pmlr.py, read-only, zero-copy
features/<run>/*.json — files only, never a socket
P1 upstream pinned by hash, vendored OUTSIDE git, recorded in NOTICE
P2 repo code is a thin adapter; upstream is never modified
P5 calibrate before any build · P6 pre-registered baseline + a NULL arm
P7 the model never sets the sign — only σ̂, size and gates
P8 fee-first: every cell reports against its own break-even bps
P9 the sidecar delivers a NUMBER over the wire; the engine never links Python
THE DOOR — one 82-byte frame, inbound only
~/multivenue/run/ai.sock · dir 0700, socket 0600, stale socket unlinked at bind · peer euid must equal ours
HMAC-SHA256 over the 64 raw cmd bytes, truncated to 16, constant-time compare · key from .env, never logged
accept order, load-bearing: len == 80 → HMAC (fail ⇒ drop the connection) → shape validate (fail ⇒ discard
the frame, keep the connection) → seq policy → ts_ns REWRITTEN to engine time → ai-cmds.pmlr → try_push
seq ≤ last ⇒ Regress, discarded; a forward jump ⇒ AcceptGap, counted, not fatal · seq lives in SQLite, so it
survives worker reconnects · TTL is checked TWICE — at ingress, then again on pop, because the clock changed
TWO DOORS INTO THE ENGINE — and they are not the same kind of thing
The sidecar decides LIVE. ai-exec keeps a 64-entry
≥ edge. An OrderIntent is submitted verbatim at the
sidecar's own px/qty — always POST-ONLY, resting.
Stale ⇒ quotes pulled, intents refused and counted.
No statistical gate. Wire shape + staleness + regime
are all that stand between a frame and an order.
The sidecar COMPILES an artifact; the engine runs it
with no AI in the loop. ≤256 rows × 128 B, 17
features, 4 combine ops, 32 832 B per table.
Only the hash128 travels — the first 16 bytes of the
artifact's SHA-256. Stage resolves the file on disk,
runs an 11-rule single-pass byte validator, and ferries
the table by value. Commit flips a ping-pong index
The gate binds here: stage-ruleset refuses unless the
worker's own backtest report matches that exact hash,
is schema-1, and gates.all_passed. No override exists.
TTL'd fair value for one sym → slot 4
TTL'd signed bias for one sym → slot 4
stage a validated table by content hash → slot 5
commit a staged hash — flips the ping-pong
sticky halt · there is no resume on the wire
one historical funding print, window seeding
restore one VM row's position at boot
declare one horizon profile's regime word
bind a rolling-family instance — one slot only
THE OFFLINE PLANE — worker, Python, globally serialized, never the hot path
serve is PARKED — no Anthropic key until
hourly, off the top of the hour
Three coded members were displaced by three new ones between 09-10 and 09-12, each on an explicit
operator ruling. The wire slot numbers did not move, so attribution reads straight through the change.
an execution lane appeared, was reviewed, and can be armed
exec-router + exec-hyperliquid landed E1–E6, then four Opus-5 review agents closed 20 blocking findings and a
zero-copy pass (in-place request body, keccak256_parts, an rx cursor) — RX 3 / TX 2 copies, the house targets.
E7 = the testnet ramp (docs/risk-policy.md "E7"); it is armed by --exec + --arm-live, never by default.
a sixth and seventh ring family
DepthTopK ×2 lanes at 192 B and OptSummary ×3 lanes joined the geometry; NUM_TICK_LANES went to 6 with
Bybit. The in-file comment still says five rings.
two model sidecars were tried and neither shipped
Both cleared the adapter pattern and both died at the numbers gate. The bay they proved out is the
reusable asset; the tenants are not, and their identities are not on this sheet.

text.tspan: read the two amber notes as load-bearing, not cosmetic.
(1) CPU pinning is wired through every ingress spawn and does nothing on the macOS deployment — the core map on this sheet describes intent, not the running process.

svg.text: (2) Fill lanes 0–2 are drained empty on every pass of the hot loop (no producer exists for them); lane 3 is fed by the Hyperliquid arm's userFills pump ONLY on an --exec boot with slot 3 live. On the default paper boot the only fill source is the paper matcher's own pump. Neither is a bug — but a reader who assumes otherwise will misread the whole sheet.

Every constant on this page was read from crates/ at HEAD 1225651 on 2026-09-19 and re-checked against the E7 review tree the same day. Where a doc comment in the tree disagreed with the code, the code is what is drawn here, and the disagreement is called out. ~/multivenue/strategy.conf is gitignored, so the enabled mask that is live right now cannot be read from source — what the wrapper permits is drawn instead.
